correctness.rationale: For n>1 odd nonsquare satisfying sigma(sigma(n))=2n-1, Fang establishes odd n and square sigma(n). Odd nonsquare implies even sigma(n), so b=v2(sigma(n)) is positive even. Since I(n)I(sigma(n))=2-1/n<2, I(sigma(n))>=I(2^b)=2-2^-b and I(n)>=product over prime support (1+1/p), the strict product bound <2^(b+1)/(2^(b+1)-1) and least prime P>2^(b+1)-1 follow. 2-adic LTE on sigma(p^a) for odd a gives v2(p+1)+v2(a+1)-1. Independent exact checks for odd primes<60 and exponents1..19 confirmed parity and LTE. No existence or nonsquare solution is claimed.

originality.rationale: Fang supplies indispensable premises square sigma(n), odd n, a special 3-divisor implication and the abundancy identity, but its inspected complete four-page text does not state the stronger b-dependent least-prime threshold or exclude 5 and 7 for a nonsquare branch. The result combines those premises with a previously unused full 2^b local index, yielding an invariant-sensitive exponential bound. The derivation uses elementary known tools and could appear as an informal earlier corollary, but no direct prior stronger statement was located.
residual_risks: The least-prime inequality is an elementary consequence once Fang premises are known; a previously unindexed remark or older informal note might have anticipated it.
No nonsquare almost superperfect n>1 is known; the sieve is an unconditional implication under a hypothetical antecedent, not an existence theorem.

value.rationale: The almost-superperfect equation is an unresolved Diophantine classification. A necessary prime-support sieve P>=11 that becomes exponentially stronger with even b is a mathematically motivated obstruction for hypothetical nonsquare solutions, not merely a parity or normalization check. The explicit prime-factor LTE formula permits further structural pruning. The result is conditional and does not resolve existence or all square solutions.
